summary: Every claim and quotation checked out. One change: the link to the Ghatak and Guinnane paper could not be opened, so it now points to the copy on Maitreesh Ghatak's LSE page.

changes.why: The Berkeley course link could not be opened or confirmed. The LSE copy is the same paper (Journal of Development Economics 60, 1999, 195-228) and supports the group-of-five design, the four lender problems and the German co-operatives figures.

notes: The Green Bank of Caraga is described by Gine and Karlan as a rural bank in the central Philippines; it is its 169 centres, not necessarily the bank's head office, that were on Leyte. The story's wording can be read either way.

Sources differ on the year of the first $27: Yunus's lecture places his discovery in the 1974 famine years, while Grameen and the Company Histories entry date the Jobra project to 1976. The story follows both sensibly.
Stiglitz's abstract says peer monitoring moves risk from the bank to the 'cosigner'; the story's 'borrowers' neighbours' is a fair paraphrase, since the cosigners in his model are neighbours.

The Wall Street Journal figures (19 per cent of loans a year overdue; half the portfolio in two northern districts) are as reported by Pearl and Phillips in 2001 and quoted by Roodman; they are journalists' figures, not Grameen's own accounts.
